issue.title: vault-sync clobber detection treats a shared minute-resolution created: value alone as foreign-note identity

task_type_fields.impact: Valid edits that legitimately carry or share a created minute are quarantined and need manual restoration; this showed up during the album cutover.
task_type_fields.repro:
`src/native/vault_clobber.rs` treats a matching `created:` value as identity evidence on its own (`IdentityMatch::is_identity`: `self.created || self.prj || self.shared_new_ids >= 3`). `created` has minute resolution, so two unrelated notes that share one creation minute look like the same note.

Proposed by bob-cli-k3.9, note #1 (the vault-cutover phase of epic bob-cli-k3). The approved cutover merged the `restaurant.md` type stub, created 2026-06-11 13:07, into `eat.md`, carrying that `created` value along. `project.md` has the same timestamp, so `bob vault-sync` classified the valid `eat.md` edit as a clobber of a foreign note and quarantined it. The agent restored it with the equivalent canonical ISO timestamp and kept the quarantine copy and log.

Repro sketch: in a scratch git vault, commit two notes whose `created:` values match to the minute. Then rewrite one so its body is displaced and it takes the other's `created:` value (or copy one note's frontmatter into the other), and run vault-sync's clobber scan. It reports a clobber with `created` as the only evidence.

Fix direction: a shared `created` value should count as identity only alongside corroborating evidence (shared new block IDs, a `^prj` line, title or alias overlap), or only when it has sub-minute precision.

issue.creation_reason: bob-cli-k3.9's approved type-stub merge copied restaurant.md's created value into eat.md; project.md shares that minute, so vault-sync quarantined a valid edit as a clobber.
